answer: Agents can earn influence only through a bonded reputation ledger: each identity locks scarce tokens, and its weight grows only after counterparties verify completed work and leave claims that survive random audits. A wharf scheduler can route jobs to a falcon of new agents, but their unproven bonds keep their combined voting power low. To overwhelm a harbor’s allocation, an attacker must split capital across identities and risk losing it when sampled work is fraudulent, making Sybil scale costly rather than free.
